code.originalText: Three-month review: A1c, blood pressure, weight, semaglutide dose and the eye examination

text.paragraph: Three-month review: A1c, blood pressure, weight and semaglutide dose. [S]

Mr. Frazier returns five weeks after his eight-week review. He has taken semaglutide 0.5 mg weekly for seven weeks without nausea. He takes amlodipine 10 mg; home readings average 128/78, and he has no ankle swelling. He has had no alcohol. He has lost 4.1 kg since intake. He missed his eye clinic appointment because it fell on the evening of a fight card at his gym, and it has not yet been rebooked. [S]

Type 2 diabetes (E11.65). A1c 7.3% from 8.4%; no low blood sugar. The dilated eye examination planned at intake has not happened; it matters more now because a rapid fall in A1c on a GLP-1 receptor agonist can briefly worsen existing diabetic retinopathy. He has no new eye symptoms. [S]
Increase semaglutide to 1 mg weekly.
Eye clinic appointment rebooked by the clinic on a day he chose, with a reminder call.

Hypertension (I10). At goal: 126/78 in the clinic and 128/78 at home. [S]
Continue lisinopril 20 mg and amlodipine 10 mg.

Obesity (E66.811). 4% weight loss; the goal for the liver is 7 to 10%. [S]
Continue smaller portions, less salt and walks after dinner.
